run_python.description: Execute Python code on the Kit main thread with full access to the Omniverse APIs (omni, carb, pxr preloaded; assign to `result` to return a value). Top-level `await` works (e.g. `await omni.kit.app.get_app().next_update_async()` to let frames run between steps). Set persistent=True with a session_id to keep variables between calls. Opening a stage (including save-as) resets every session; the next call says so. For work longer than a few seconds pass background=true: it returns a job_id at once for job_status / job_cancel, instead of polling with more calls.

code.description: Python code to execute on Kit's main thread

session_id.description: Session identifier for persistent execution. Use the same ID across calls to share state. Defaults to 'default'.

persistent.description: If true, variables persist across calls with the same session_id. The reply lists only the names this call added or rebound (session_vars) and the total (session_var_count).

background.description: Run as a job and return its job_id at once. The code must await (e.g. `await omni.kit.app.get_app().next_update_async()` in its loop) and must not pump the app itself. A `job` object is preloaded: job.report(fraction, text) sets progress, job.checkpoint() raises once job_cancel was called. Follow with job_status(job_id, wait_s=30); `result` and prints come back there.

label.description: With background: a short name shown by job_status.

status.description: Where am I, in one call: the bridge that answered (pid, port, app, readiness), every bridge advertised on this machine, the current stage's session_id and stage_id with the timeline state, and running jobs. With nothing running it says so and names the next call, instead of failing. Call it once before the first simulator action; there is no need to repeat it between calls.

detail.description: true: the full bridge identity as well (namespaces, what is running and waiting, extension source). Default false: the short reply.

job_status.description: Check a background job in this Kit; with no job_id, list the jobs. run_python(background=true), sim__simulation__run and sim__trajectory__replay return a job_id. Gives state (running, succeeded, failed, cancelled), elapsed_s, progress, the last output and, when finished, the result or error. The list is newest first. Through the MCP server it also takes an Isaac Lab or script job_id (isaaclab__train, run_script, ...), with no bridge needed.

job_id.description: job_id from the call that started the work. Omit to list jobs.

wait_s.description: Wait up to this many seconds (0-60; a larger value waits 60) for the job to end before answering, instead of polling.

job_cancel.description: Stop a background job. job_id comes from the call that started it. It ends at its next step and cleans up after itself; confirm with job_status. Through the MCP server it also stops an Isaac Lab or script job.
